chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
"And prepare for them whatever force you can muster."
He said: "Among it is dyeing with black.
And indeed a man entered upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with his beard dyed yellow, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: "How fine this is."
Then he entered upon him after this having dyed with henna, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله smiled and said: "This is better than that."
Then he entered upon him after that having dyed with black, so he laughed toward him and said: "This is better than that and that."

key_terms.الْخِضَابُ: dyeing, especially of the hair or beard
key_terms.قُوَّةٍ: force, strength, or means of preparedness

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام interpret "And prepare for them whatever force you can muster" in relation to dyeing with black?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains the verse about preparing strength as including outward forms of readiness and appearance, such as dyeing with black. The report then cites the approval of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله for successive forms of beard dyeing, with black presented as the best among those mentioned.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.282 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) commented on the verse of Allah (swt), the Exalted, "And prepare for them whatever force you can muster" (Surah Al-Anfal; 8:60).
Imam (as) said: "Among it is dyeing with black”.
(From Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) );
A man entered upon the Messenger of Allah (sw) with his beard dyed yellow (light color), and the Messenger of Allah (sw) said to him, "How good this is."
Then he entered again after that with his beard dyed with henna (reddish color), and the Messenger of Allah (sw) smiled and said: "This is better than the previous."
Then he entered again after having dyed it black, and the Prophet smiled and said:
"This is better than both of the previous”.
